name: AI D12 - New money
description: Hourly: Google News for freshly funded UK/IE startups, Sonnet extracts the raise, adds net-new accounts (or attaches funding to existing ones). No email: T1 alerts on Telegram with Mine / Owned. Enrichment and why-now follow on the normal schedules.

parameters.text:
=You read one news headline and snippet and extract a funding round, if there is one. Return ONLY the JSON requested.

Headline: {{ $json.title }}
Snippet: {{ $json.text }}
Source: {{ $json.source }} Date: {{ $json.date }}

Rules:
- is_raise is true only when ONE named company raised equity or venture money (seed, pre-seed, Series A/B/C, growth or strategic investment, angel round). Grants, government or Innovate UK awards, loans, charity fundraising, funds raised BY an investor (a VC closing a fund), accelerator cohorts, and round-ups listing several companies are is_raise false.
- company: the company's name as written, without Ltd or Limited. domain: the company's website domain if it appears in the text, else an empty string.
- amount as written (for example 4m pounds, $20 million) or empty. stage: seed, pre-seed, Series A, Series B, growth, angel or unknown.
- event_date: YYYY-MM-DD from the article date.
- uk_or_ie: true only if the company is based in the UK or Ireland (the article says so, or the city named is in the UK or Ireland). If unclear, false.
- is_ai: true if the company's product is AI or machine learning.
- location: city or country as stated.
- summary: one sentence, facts only.
- confidence 0 to 1 that company, amount and location are right.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"is_raise":true,"company":"Acme","domain":"acme.com","amount":"4m pounds","stage":"Series A","event_date":"2026-10-12","location":"London","uk_or_ie":true,"is_ai":true,"summary":"Acme raised a Series A led by X to expand into Europe","confidence":0.9}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_name: $json.company, p_domain: $json.domain, p_amount: $json.amount, p_stage: $json.stage, p_url: $json.url, p_event_date: $json.event_date, p_is_ai: $json.is_ai, p_summary: $json.summary, p_location: $json.location }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ p_url: $('Keep?').item.json.url, p_outcome: (() => { try { return JSON.parse($json.body)[0].outcome; } catch (e) { return 'error'; } })(), p_company: $('Keep?').item.json.company }) }}
